title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Chemical Reaction
text:
Chemical Reaction

Key terms: Reactants, Products, Chemical Change

A chemical reaction is a process where one or more substances (reactants) transform into one or more different substances (products). This change can be observed through changes in state, color, gas evolution, or temperature.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Chemical Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Word Equation
text:
Word Equation

Key terms: Reactants, Products, Arrow

A word equation represents a chemical reaction using words instead of chemical formulas. It shows reactants on the left side and products on the right side, separated by an arrow.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Word Equation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Chemical Formula Equation
text:
Chemical Formula Equation

Key terms: Chemical Formula, Balanced Equation

A chemical formula equation represents a chemical reaction using chemical formulas instead of words. It must be balanced to show the same number of atoms of each element on both sides of the equation.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Chemical Formula Equation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Balancing Chemical Equations
text:
Balancing Chemical Equations

Key terms: Coefficients, Balanced Equation

Balancing a chemical equation involves adding coefficients to the reactants and products to ensure that the number of atoms of each element is the same on both sides of the equation.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Balancing Chemical Equations in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Combination Reaction
text:
Combination Reaction

Key terms: Reactants, Product, Combination

A combination reaction is a type of chemical reaction where two or more substances combine to form a single product. An example is the reaction between calcium oxide and water to form calcium hydroxide.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Combination Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Exothermic Reaction
text:
Exothermic Reaction

Key terms: Heat, Products, Exothermic

An exothermic reaction is a type of chemical reaction where heat is released along with the formation of products. Examples include burning of coal and respiration.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Exothermic Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Decomposition Reaction
text:
Decomposition Reaction

Key terms: Substance, Products, Decomposition

A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction where a single substance breaks down into two or more different substances. An example is the decomposition of lead nitrate into lead oxide and nitrogen dioxide.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Decomposition Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Decomposition Reaction
text:
Decomposition Reaction

Key terms: decomposition, heat, light

A reaction where a single substance breaks down into simpler substances, often with heat or light.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Decomposition Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Thermal Decomposition
text:
Thermal Decomposition

Key terms: thermal, heat, decomposition

A type of decomposition reaction that occurs with the application of heat.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Thermal Decomposition in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Displacement Reaction
text:
Displacement Reaction

A reaction where one element displaces another from its compound.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Displacement Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

Precipitation Reaction

A reaction that produces an insoluble substance (precipitate) in a solution.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Precipitation Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

Oxidation and Reduction

Reactions where substances gain or lose oxygen or hydrogen, leading to oxidation or reduction.

Oxidising Agent

A substance that causes another substance to lose electrons (get oxidised).

text:
Reducing Agent

A substance that causes another substance to gain electrons (get reduced).

metadata.subject: Science

text:
Corrosion

The damage of a material (usually metal) by a chemical or electrochemical reaction.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Corrosion in Grade 10 Science.

text:
Balancing Chemical Equations

Key terms: balance, coefficients, atoms

To balance a chemical equation, the number of atoms of each element on the reactant and product sides must be equal. This is done by adjusting the coefficients in front of the formulas.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Balancing Chemical Equations in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Writing Balanced Chemical Equations
text:
Writing Balanced Chemical Equations

Writing a balanced chemical equation involves representing a chemical reaction with the correct formulas and coefficients to show the number of atoms of each element on both sides of the equation.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Writing Balanced Chemical Equations in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Identifying Types of Reactions
text:
Identifying Types of Reactions

Key terms: precipitation, decomposition, combustion

Chemical reactions can be classified into different types such as precipitation, decomposition, combustion, etc. based on the changes that occur during the reaction.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Identifying Types of Reactions in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions
text:
Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions

Key terms: exothermic, endothermic, heat energy

Exothermic reactions release heat energy, while endothermic reactions absorb heat energy. Examples include combustion reactions (exothermic) and photosynthesis (endothermic).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Respiration as an Exothermic Reaction
text:
Respiration as an Exothermic Reaction

Key terms: respiration, exothermic, glucose

Respiration is an exothermic reaction because it releases energy, which is used by the body for various functions. This energy is released when glucose is broken down in the presence of oxygen.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Respiration as an Exothermic Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Decomposition and Combination Reactions
text:
Decomposition and Combination Reactions

Key terms: decomposition, combination, compound

Decomposition reactions involve the breakdown of a compound into simpler substances, while combination reactions involve the combination of two or more substances to form a single compound.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Decomposition and Combination Reactions in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Displacement and Double Displacement Reactions
text:
Displacement and Double Displacement Reactions

Key terms: displacement, double displacement, ions

Displacement reactions involve the replacement of one element by another in a compound, while double displacement reactions involve the exchange of ions between two compounds.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Displacement and Double Displacement Reactions in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Oxidation and Reduction
text:
Oxidation and Reduction

Key terms: oxidation, reduction, redox

Oxidation involves the loss of electrons or an increase in oxidation state, while reduction involves the gain of electrons or a decrease in oxidation state. These processes occur simultaneously in a redox reaction.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Oxidation and Reduction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Acids and Bases in Everyday Life
text:
Acids and Bases in Everyday Life

Key terms: acid, base, litmus

Acids and bases are present in many everyday substances. Acids are sour and can nullify the effect of bases, which are bitter. Indicators like litmus can help identify acids and bases.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Acids and Bases in Everyday Life
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Acids and Bases in Everyday Life in Grade 10 Science.

text:
Acids Change Litmus Color to Red

Key terms: acid, litmus, H+

Acids turn blue litmus red, indicating the presence of hydrogen ions (H+). This is a key property of acids.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Acids Change Litmus Color to Red

Bases Change Litmus Color to Blue

Key terms: base, litmus, OH-

Bases turn red litmus blue, indicating the presence of hydroxide ions (OH-). This is a key property of bases.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Bases Change Litmus Color to Blue

text:
Acids and Bases React with Each Other

Acids and bases react with each other to form a salt and water. This reaction is called neutralisation.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Acids and Bases React with Each Other in Grade 10 Science.

text:
Acids React with Metals to Produce Hydrogen Gas

Key terms: hydrogen gas, salt, metal

Acids react with metals to produce hydrogen gas and a salt. The reaction can be summarised as: Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen gas.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Acids React with Metals to Produce Hydrogen Gas
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Acids React with Metals to Produce Hydrogen Gas in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Acids and Bases React with Metal Carbonates and Hydrogencarbonates
text:
Acids and Bases React with Metal Carbonates and Hydrogencarbonates

Key terms: carbon dioxide, salt, metal carbonate

Acids react with metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates to produce a salt, carbon dioxide, and water. The reaction can be summarised as: Acid + Metal Carbonate/Hydrogencarbonate → Salt + Carbon Dioxide + Water.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Acids and Bases React with Metal Carbonates and Hydrogencarbonates
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Acids and Bases React with Metal Carbonates and Hydrogencarbonates in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Acids and Bases React with Each Other to Form Salts and Water
text:
Acids and Bases React with Each Other to Form Salts and Water

Key terms: salt, water, neutralisation

Acids and bases react with each other to form a salt and water. The general reaction can be written as: Base + Acid → Salt + Water.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Acids and Bases React with Each Other to Form Salts and Water
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Acids and Bases React with Each Other to Form Salts and Water in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Acid-Base Neutralization
text:
Acid-Base Neutralization

Key terms: Acid, Base, Salt, Neutralization

Acids and bases react to form salts and water, with the base providing hydroxide ions (OH-) and the acid providing hydrogen ions (H+).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Acid-Base Neutralization in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | pH Scale
text:
pH Scale

Key terms: pH, Acidic, Basic, Neutral

pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of a solution, with values ranging from 0 (very acidic) to 14 (very basic), and 7 being neutral.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to pH Scale in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Strong vs Weak Acids/Bases
text:
Strong vs Weak Acids/Bases

Key terms: Strong Acid, Weak Acid, Strong Base, Weak Base

Strong acids/bases completely dissociate in water, while weak acids/bases only partially dissociate. Strong acids/bases are stronger than weak ones.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Strong vs Weak Acids/Bases in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Acid Rain
text:
Acid Rain

Key terms: Acid Rain, pH, Pollution

Acid rain is rainwater with a pH lower than 5.6, caused by sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning fossil fuels reacting with water and oxygen in the atmosphere.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Acid Rain in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Soil pH and Plant Growth
text:
Soil pH and Plant Growth

Key terms: Soil pH, Plant Growth, Ideal Conditions

Plants require specific pH ranges for healthy growth. The pH of soil can be tested to determine the ideal conditions for plant growth.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Soil pH and Plant Growth in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Tooth Decay and pH
text:
Tooth Decay and pH

Key terms: Tooth Decay, pH, Toothpaste

Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5, causing tooth enamel to corrode. Using basic toothpastes can help prevent this.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Tooth Decay and pH in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Salts from Acids and Bases
text:
Salts from Acids and Bases

Key terms: Salt, Acid, Base, Neutral

Salts are formed when acids react with bases, with the salt's nature (acidic, basic, or neutral) depending on the strength of the original acid and base.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Salts from Acids and Bases in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Chlor-Alkali Process
text:
Chlor-Alkali Process

Key terms: Chlor-Alkali Process, Sodium Hydroxide, Chlorine Gas, Hydrogen Gas

Electrolysis of sodium chloride (brine) produces sodium hydroxide, chlorine gas, and hydrogen gas, which are all useful products.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Chlor-Alkali Process in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Baking Soda Uses
text:
Baking Soda Uses

Key terms: baking soda, carbon dioxide, antacid

Baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate) is used in baking to make bread and cakes rise, in antacids to neutralize stomach acid, and in soda-acid fire extinguishers to produce carbon dioxide.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Baking Soda Uses in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Washing Soda Uses
text:
Washing Soda Uses

Key terms: washing soda, sodium carbonate, hardness of water

Washing soda (sodium carbonate) is used in glass, soap, and paper industries, in manufacturing sodium compounds like borax, as a cleaning agent, and for removing permanent hardness of water.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Washing Soda Uses in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Water of Crystallisation
text:
Water of Crystallisation

Key terms: water of crystallisation, salt, crystal

Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt. It can be removed by heating, and adding water can restore the original crystal form.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Water of Crystallisation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Plaster of Paris
text:
Plaster of Paris

Key terms: Plaster of Paris, gypsum, calcium sulphate hemihydrate

Plaster of Paris is obtained by heating gypsum, which loses water molecules and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate. It is used for supporting fractured bones and in making toys and decorative materials.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Plaster of Paris in Grade 10 Science.

text:
Acid-Base Indicators

Acid-base indicators are dyes or mixtures of dyes used to indicate the presence of acids and bases by changing color in response to a change in pH.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Acid-Base Indicators in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Neutralisation Reaction
text:
Neutralisation Reaction

A neutralisation reaction is a chemical reaction in which an acid and a base react to form a salt and water. This reaction can be used to test the strength of acids and bases.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Neutralisation Reaction in Grade 10 Science.

Acids and Bases in Everyday Life

Acids and bases have various uses in everyday life and industries, such as in baking, cleaning, and manufacturing processes.

The pH scale is a measure of the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, with a pH of 7 being neutral, less than 7 being acidic, and more than 7 being basic.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to pH Scale in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Metallic Lustre
text:
Metallic Lustre

Key terms: metallic lustre, metal samples, sandpaper

Metals in their pure state have a shiny surface, called metallic lustre. This can be observed by cleaning the surface of metal samples with sandpaper and noting their appearance.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Metallic Lustre in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Malleability of Metals
text:
Malleability of Metals

Key terms: malleability, metals, hammer

Some metals can be beaten into thin sheets, a property called malleability. This can be demonstrated by trying to cut metals with a sharp knife and observing the change in their shape when struck with a hammer.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Malleability of Metals in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Ductility of Metals
text:
Ductility of Metals

Key terms: ductility, metals, wires

Metals can be drawn into thin wires, a property called ductility. This can be observed by listing the metals whose wires are commonly used in daily life.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ductility of Metals in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Conductivity of Metals
text:
Conductivity of Metals

Key terms: conductivity, metals, heat, electricity

Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity. This can be demonstrated by heating a metal wire and observing its behavior, as well as by setting up an electric circuit with a metal sample and a bulb.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Conductivity of Metals in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Reactivity of Metals with Oxygen
text:
Reactivity of Metals with Oxygen

Key terms: reactivity, metals, oxygen, metal oxides

Metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides. The rate of reaction varies among metals, which can be observed by burning metal samples in air and collecting the products.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Reactivity of Metals with Oxygen in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Reactivity of Metals with Water
text:
Reactivity of Metals with Water

Key terms: reactivity, metals, water, hydrogen gas

Metals react with water to produce a metal oxide and hydrogen gas. The reactivity varies among metals, which can be observed by placing metal samples in cold and hot water, and exposing them to steam.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Reactivity of Metals with Water in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Reactivity of Metals with Acids
text:
Reactivity of Metals with Acids

Key terms: reactivity, metals, acids, hydrogen gas

Metals react with acids to give a salt and hydrogen gas. The rate of reaction varies among metals, which can be observed by placing metal samples in dilute hydrochloric acid and noting the rate of bubble formation and temperature change.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Reactivity of Metals with Acids in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Reactivity of Metals with Dilute HCl
text:
Reactivity of Metals with Dilute HCl

Key terms: dilute hydrochloric acid, hydrogen gas, reactivity

Metals react with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas and a salt. The rate of reaction and heat produced depend on the metal's reactivity. Magnesium reacts fastest and most exothermically, while copper does not react.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Reactivity of Metals with Dilute HCl
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Reactivity of Metals with Dilute HCl in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Displacement Reactions
text:
Displacement Reactions

Key terms: displacement reaction, reactivity series

A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive metal from its compound in solution or molten form. This is known as a displacement reaction.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Displacement Reactions in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Aqua Regia
text:
Aqua Regia

Key terms: aqua regia, gold, platinum

A mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and nitric acid in a 3:1 ratio can dissolve gold and platinum, which neither acid can dissolve alone. It is highly corrosive and fuming.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Aqua Regia in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Extraction of Metals
text:
Extraction of Metals

Key terms: ore, extraction, reduction

Metals are extracted from ores using various methods depending on their reactivity. Less reactive metals can be obtained by heating their ores, while more reactive metals require reduction processes like electrolysis.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Extraction of Metals in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Enrichment of Ores
text:
Enrichment of Ores

Key terms: ore, gangue, enrichment

Ores are enriched by removing impurities (gangue) using techniques based on differences in physical or chemical properties between the ore and gangue.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Enrichment of Ores in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Ionic Compounds
text:
Ionic Compounds

Key terms: ionic compound, electrovalent compound, melting point, boiling point

Ionic compounds are formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal. They are solids, have high melting and boiling points, are soluble in water, and conduct electricity in the molten state or in aqueous solution.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ionic Compounds in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Electron-dot Structures
text:
Electron-dot Structures

Key terms: electron-dot structure, ionic compound, electron transfer

Electron-dot structures represent the arrangement of electrons in the outermost shell of an atom. They can be used to show the formation of ionic compounds by electron transfer.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Electron-dot Structures in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Occurrence of Metals
text:
Occurrence of Metals

Key terms: mineral, ore, occurrence

Metals are found in the earth's crust as minerals or ores. Some are found in the free state, while others are found combined with other elements as oxides, sulphides, or carbonates.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Occurrence of Metals in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Roasting and Calcination of Metal Ores
text:
Roasting and Calcination of Metal Ores

Key terms: Roasting, Calcination, Oxidation

Roasting and calcination are processes to convert metal sulphides and carbonates into oxides before reduction. Roasting uses excess air, while calcination uses limited air.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Roasting and Calcination of Metal Ores
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Roasting and Calcination of Metal Ores in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Reduction of Metal Oxides
text:
Reduction of Metal Oxides

Key terms: Reduction, Reducing Agent, Displacement Reaction

Metal oxides can be reduced to metals using reducing agents like carbon or displacement reactions using highly reactive metals like sodium, calcium, or aluminium.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Reduction of Metal Oxides in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Electrolytic Reduction of Metals
text:
Electrolytic Reduction of Metals

Key terms: Electrolytic Reduction, Cathode, Anode

Metals high up in the reactivity series are obtained by electrolytic reduction, where the metal is deposited at the cathode and chlorine is liberated at the anode.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electrolytic Reduction of Metals in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Electrolytic Refining of Metals
text:
Electrolytic Refining of Metals

Key terms: Electrolytic Refining, Anode, Cathode, Electrolyte

Electrolytic refining is used to purify impure metals. The impure metal is made the anode, and a pure metal strip is made the cathode. The electrolyte is a solution of the metal salt.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrolytic Refining of Metals in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Corrosion of Iron
text:
Corrosion of Iron

Key terms: Corrosion, Rust, Prevention of Corrosion

Iron rusts when exposed to moist air for a long time, forming a brown flaky substance called rust. This can be prevented by painting, oiling, greasing, galvanising, chrome plating, anodising, or making alloys.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Corrosion of Iron in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Alloys
text:
Alloys

Key terms: Alloy, Homogeneous Mixture, Properties of Alloys

An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a non-metal. Alloys have different properties than the individual metals and can be used to improve the properties of a metal.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Alloys in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Carbon's Importance
text:
Carbon's Importance

Key terms: carbon, versatile, living structures

Carbon is a versatile element found in many things we use daily, like food, clothes, and medicines. It's also the basis for all living structures. Despite its small amount in nature, its importance is immense due to its unique properties.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Carbon's Importance in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Covalent Bonding in Carbon
text:
Covalent Bonding in Carbon

Key terms: covalent bond, electron sharing, noble gas configuration

Carbon forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons with other carbon atoms or atoms of other elements. This allows both atoms to attain a noble gas configuration, making carbon compounds stable and non-conductive.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Covalent Bonding in Carbon in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Catenation in Carbon
text:
Catenation in Carbon

Key terms: catenation, carbon chains, carbon rings

Carbon's ability to form bonds with other carbon atoms, called catenation, allows it to create long chains, branched chains, or even carbon rings. This leads to a vast number of carbon compounds.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Catenation in Carbon in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Saturated and Unsaturated Carbon Compounds
text:
Saturated and Unsaturated Carbon Compounds

Key terms: saturated compounds, unsaturated compounds, reactivity

Carbon compounds with only single bonds between carbon atoms are called saturated, while those with double or triple bonds are unsaturated. Saturated compounds are less reactive than unsaturated ones.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Saturated and Unsaturated Carbon Compounds in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Allotropes of Carbon
text:
Allotropes of Carbon

Key terms: allotropes, diamond, graphite

Puberty

The male and female reproductive systems, including organs and hormones involved in the production and transfer of gametes.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Fertilization and Embryo Development
text:
Fertilization and Embryo Development

Key terms: zygote, embryo, fetus, placenta

Fertilization occurs when sperm meets the egg. The fertilized egg (zygote) divides and forms an embryo, which implants in the uterus and grows into a fetus. The mother's body prepares the uterus each month to receive and nurture the growing embryo.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Menstruation
text:
Menstruation

Key terms: menstruation, menstrual flow, uterine lining

If the egg is not fertilized, it dies after one day. The uterine lining, which thickens monthly to nourish a potential embryo, breaks down and is shed as menstrual flow.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Menstruation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Sexual Maturation and Responsibility
text:
Sexual Maturation and Responsibility

Key terms: sexual maturation, sexual health, responsibility

Sexual maturation is a gradual process that does not necessarily mean the body or mind is ready for sexual acts or parenthood. Making choices about sexual health can be influenced by various pressures.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Sexual Maturation and Responsibility in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs)
text:
Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs)

Key terms: STDs, condom, transmission prevention

STDs can be transmitted through sexual contact. Using a condom can help prevent the transmission of some STDs, but it is not a foolproof method.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs) in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Contraception
text:
Contraception

Key terms: contraception, mechanical barrier, hormonal balance

Contraception methods aim to prevent pregnancy by creating a mechanical barrier or altering hormonal balances. They can have side effects and may not protect against STDs.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Contraception in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Population Growth Concerns
text:
Population Growth Concerns

The size of the human population can impact living standards. Reckless female foeticides can lead to an imbalanced sex ratio, which is a concern for society.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Population Growth Concerns in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Variations in Reproduction
text:
Variations in Reproduction

Key terms: reproduction, variations, inheritance, survival

Reproductive processes create new individuals that are similar but have subtle differences. These variations can be inherited and may increase an individual's chances of survival.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Variations in Reproduction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Dominant and Recessive Traits
text:
Dominant and Recessive Traits

Key terms: dominant, recessive, traits, genes

Some traits are dominant, meaning they are expressed even if an individual has one copy of the gene. Recessive traits only show up if an individual has two copies of the gene.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Dominant and Recessive Traits in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Independent Inheritance of Traits
text:
Independent Inheritance of Traits

Key terms: independent, inheritance, traits, combinations

Traits can be inherited independently, meaning that different traits can be passed down separately, leading to new combinations in offspring.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Independent Inheritance of Traits in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Sex Determination in Humans
text:
Sex Determination in Humans

Key terms: sex chromosomes, X, Y, inheritance

In humans, sex is determined by the X and Y chromosomes. A child inherits an X chromosome from their mother, and a Y chromosome from their father determines the child's sex.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Sex Determination in Humans in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Inheritance of Traits
text:
Inheritance of Traits

Key terms: trait, gene, dominant, recessive

Traits can be inherited from parents to offspring. In sexually reproducing organisms, each individual has two copies of genes for the same trait, one from each parent. If these copies are different, one trait is dominant and the other is recessive.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Inheritance of Traits in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Independent Assortment of Traits
text:
Independent Assortment of Traits

Key terms: independent assortment, trait, offspring

Traits in an individual can be inherited separately, leading to new combinations of traits in the offspring of sexual reproduction.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Independent Assortment of Traits in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Sex Determination in Humans
text:
Sex Determination in Humans

Key terms: sex chromosomes, X chromosome, Y chromosome

In humans, the sex of a child is determined by the sex chromosomes inherited from the father. An X chromosome results in a girl, while a Y chromosome results in a boy.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Sex Determination in Humans in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Mendelian Crossing Experiment
text:
Mendelian Crossing Experiment

Key terms: Mendelian crossing, progeny, genetic make-up

A Mendelian experiment involved crossing tall pea plants with violet flowers and short pea plants with white flowers. The resulting progeny had violet flowers but were almost half short, suggesting a specific genetic make-up of the tall parent.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Mendelian Crossing Experiment in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Dominance and Recessiveness in Eye Color
text:
Dominance and Recessiveness in Eye Color

Key terms: dominance, recessiveness, eye color

A study found that children with light-colored eyes often have parents with light-colored eyes. However, this does not necessarily indicate whether the light eye color trait is dominant or recessive, as more information is needed.

metadata.topic: Dominance and Recessiveness in Eye Color
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Dominance and Recessiveness in Eye Color in Grade 10 Science.

Project: Dominant Coat Color in Dogs

A project could be designed to determine the dominant coat color in dogs by observing the offspring of different crosses and recording their coat colors.

text:
Equal Genetic Contribution of Parents

Key terms: equal genetic contribution, meiosis, chromosomes

In sexual reproduction, the equal genetic contribution of male and female parents to the offspring is ensured through the process of meiosis, where each parent provides one set of chromosomes to the offspring.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Equal Genetic Contribution of Parents in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Light Propagation
text:
Light Propagation

Light travels in straight lines, but can bend around small objects (diffraction) and behave like both waves and particles.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Light Propagation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Reflection of Light
text:
Reflection of Light

Key terms: angle of incidence, angle of reflection, laws of reflection

Light bounces off surfaces, following the laws of reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, and the incident ray, normal, and reflected ray lie in the same plane.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Reflection of Light in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Image Formation by Plane Mirrors
text:
Image Formation by Plane Mirrors

Key terms: virtual image, erect, laterally inverted

Plane mirrors form virtual, erect, and laterally inverted images of the same size as the object, located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Image Formation by Plane Mirrors in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Spherical Mirrors
text:
Spherical Mirrors

Key terms: concave mirror, convex mirror, pole, center of curvature, radius of curvature

Spherical mirrors can be concave (curved inwards) or convex (curved outwards), with a pole (center of the reflecting surface), center of curvature (center of the sphere), and radius of curvature (radius of the sphere).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Spherical Mirrors in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Principal Focus and Focal Length
text:
Principal Focus and Focal Length

Key terms: principal focus, focal length

The principal focus is the point where light rays converge or appear to diverge from after reflection. The focal length is the distance between the pole and the principal focus.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Principal Focus and Focal Length in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Image Formation by Spherical Mirrors
text:
Image Formation by Spherical Mirrors

Key terms: real image, virtual image, inverted, erect, magnified, diminished

The nature, position, and size of the image formed by a spherical mirror depend on the position of the object. Images can be real or virtual, inverted or erect, and magnified, diminished, or the same size as the object.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Image Formation by Spherical Mirrors in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Ray Diagrams for Image Formation
text:
Ray Diagrams for Image Formation

Key terms: ray diagram, principal axis, focus, center of curvature, pole

Ray diagrams help locate the image of an object by tracing the paths of reflected rays. Key rays include those parallel to the principal axis, passing through the focus, passing through the center of curvature, and incident obliquely at the pole.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Ray Diagrams for Image Formation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Laws of Reflection
text:
Laws of Reflection

Key terms: angle of incidence, angle of reflection, normal

When light reflects off a smooth, non-absorbing surface, the angle of incidence (∠i) equals the angle of reflection (∠r), and both are measured from the normal at the point of incidence.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Laws of Reflection in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Image Formation by Concave Mirror
text:
Image Formation by Concave Mirror

Key terms: concave mirror, real image, inverted, magnified

A concave mirror forms a real, inverted, and magnified image of an object placed in front of it, between the focus and the mirror. The image size and position depend on the object's distance from the mirror.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Image Formation by Concave Mirror in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Image Formation by Convex Mirror
text:
Image Formation by Convex Mirror

Key terms: convex mirror, virtual image, erect, diminished

A convex mirror forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image of an object placed in front of it, behind the mirror. The image is always upright and smaller than the object.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Image Formation by Convex Mirror in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Refraction of Light
text:
Refraction of Light

Key terms: refraction, optical density, refractive index

When light travels from one medium to another with different optical densities, it changes direction, a phenomenon known as refraction. The extent of refraction depends on the refractive indices of the media.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Refraction of Light in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Snell's Law
text:
Snell's Law

Key terms: Snell's law, refractive index, angle of incidence, angle of refraction

Snell's law describes the relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction when light passes through a boundary between two different media, such as air and glass. It is expressed as n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2), where n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ1 and θ2 are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Snell's Law in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Total Internal Reflection
text:
Total Internal Reflection

Key terms: total internal reflection, critical angle

Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle, causing the light to reflect back into the denser medium without any refraction.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Total Internal Reflection in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Refraction of Light through a Rectangular Glass Slab
text:
Refraction of Light through a Rectangular Glass Slab

Key terms: refraction, normal, incident ray, emergent ray

When light passes from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal. The extent of bending is equal and opposite at both interfaces of the slab, causing the light to emerge parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideward.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Refraction of Light through a Rectangular Glass Slab
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Refraction of Light through a Rectangular Glass Slab in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Laws of Refraction
text:
Laws of Refraction

Key terms: Snell's law, angle of incidence, angle of refraction

The incident ray, refracted ray, and normal at the point of incidence lie in the same plane. The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is a constant (Snell's law) for a given pair of media and light color.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Laws of Refraction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Refractive Index
text:
Refractive Index

Key terms: refractive index, speed of light, vacuum

The refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in that medium. It determines the extent of bending of light as it enters a new medium.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Refractive Index in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Optical Density
text:
Optical Density

Key terms: optical density, refractive index, rarer medium

A medium with a larger refractive index is optically denser than one with a smaller refractive index. Light travels slower in optically denser media and bends towards the normal when entering from a rarer medium.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Optical Density in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Converging and Diverging Lenses
text:
Converging and Diverging Lenses

Key terms: convex lens, concave lens, converging, diverging

Convex lenses are converging lenses that thicken towards the middle and converge light rays, while concave lenses are diverging lenses that thin towards the middle and diverge light rays.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Converging and Diverging Lenses in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Image Formation by Lenses
text:
Image Formation by Lenses

Key terms: real image, virtual image, inverted, erect

Convex lenses form real, inverted images, while concave lenses form virtual, erect images. The nature, position, and relative size of the image depend on the object's position relative to the lens.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Image Formation by Lenses in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Image Formation by Concave Lens
text:
Image Formation by Concave Lens

Key terms: concave lens, virtual image, erect image, diminished image

A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image, regardless of the object's position. The image is always on the same side of the lens as the object.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Image Formation by Concave Lens in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Ray Diagrams for Lenses
text:
Ray Diagrams for Lenses

Key terms: ray diagrams, principal axis, principal focus, optical center

Ray diagrams help study the nature, position, and relative size of images formed by lenses. Key rays include: parallel to principal axis, through principal focus, and through optical center.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Ray Diagrams for Lenses in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Sign Convention for Spherical Lenses
text:
Sign Convention for Spherical Lenses

Key terms: sign convention, focal length, convex lens, concave lens

For lenses, follow the sign convention similar to spherical mirrors. Focal length is positive for convex lenses and negative for concave lenses. Take care of signs for u, v, f, h, and h' while solving problems.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Sign Convention for Spherical Lenses in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Lens Formula and Magnification
text:
Lens Formula and Magnification

Key terms: lens formula, magnification, object-distance, image-distance, focal length

The lens formula (1/v - 1/u = 1/f) relates object-distance, image-distance, and focal length. Magnification (m = h'/h or m = v/u) is the ratio of image height to object height.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Lens Formula and Magnification in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Power of a Lens
text:
Power of a Lens

Key terms: power of a lens, focal length, dioptre, converge, diverge

The power of a lens (P = 1/f) is the reciprocal of its focal length. It's a measure of the lens's ability to converge or diverge light. The SI unit is dioptre (D).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Power of a Lens in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Human Eye Structure and Function
text:
Human Eye Structure and Function

Key terms: retina, lens, accommodation

The human eye is like a camera, with a lens that focuses light onto a light-sensitive screen called the retina. The lens can change shape to focus on objects at different distances, a process called accommodation.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Human Eye Structure and Function in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Power of Accommodation
text:
Power of Accommodation

Key terms: focal length, ciliary muscles

The power of accommodation is the eye's ability to change the focal length of the lens to focus on objects at different distances. This allows us to see objects clearly, whether they are near or far.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Power of Accommodation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Defects of Vision
text:
Defects of Vision

Key terms: myopia, hypermetropia, presbyopia

Defects of vision, such as myopia (nearsightedness), hypermetropia (farsightedness), and presbyopia, occur when the eye's lens cannot focus light properly onto the retina. These defects can be corrected using spherical lenses.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Defects of Vision in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Refraction of Light Through a Prism
text:
Refraction of Light Through a Prism

Key terms: refraction, spectrum

Light refracts, or bends, as it passes through a prism. This causes the light to change direction and split into a spectrum of colors.

metadata.topic: Refraction of Light Through a Prism
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Refraction of Light Through a Prism in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Dispersion of White Light by a Prism
text:
Dispersion of White Light by a Prism

Key terms: dispersion, wavelength

White light is made up of a range of colors, each with a different wavelength. When white light passes through a prism, it is dispersed, or separated, into a spectrum of colors.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Dispersion of White Light by a Prism
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Dispersion of White Light by a Prism in Grade 10 Science.

Dispersion of Light

The splitting of white light into its component colors, creating a spectrum. Different colors bend at different angles when passing through a prism.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Dispersion of Light in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Rainbow Formation
text:
Rainbow Formation

Key terms: rainbow, dispersion, sunlight

A rainbow is a natural spectrum caused by the dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets in the atmosphere.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rainbow Formation in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Atmospheric Refraction
text:
Atmospheric Refraction

Key terms: refraction, twinkling of stars, sunrise, sunset

The bending of light as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere, causing phenomena like the twinkling of stars and the advance of sunrise and delayed sunset.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Atmospheric Refraction in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Tyndall Effect
text:
Tyndall Effect

Key terms: scattering, colloidal particles, Tyndall effect

The scattering of light by colloidal particles, making the path of light visible. Fine particles scatter blue light more strongly than red light.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Tyndall Effect in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Blue Sky
text:
Blue Sky

Key terms: blue sky, scattering, air molecules

The blue color of the sky is due to the scattering of blue light by molecules of air and other fine particles in the atmosphere.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Blue Sky in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Accommodation of the Eye
text:
Accommodation of the Eye

Key terms: accommodation, focal length, eye

The ability of the eye to focus on both near and distant objects by adjusting its focal length.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Accommodation of the Eye in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Near Point of the Eye
text:
Near Point of the Eye

The smallest distance at which the eye can see objects clearly without strain, approximately 25 cm for a young adult with normal vision.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Near Point of the Eye in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Refractive Defects of Vision
text:
Refractive Defects of Vision

Key terms: myopia, hypermetropia, presbyopia, vision

Common vision problems include myopia (nearsightedness), hypermetropia (farsightedness), and presbyopia (age-related loss of accommodation).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Refractive Defects of Vision in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Electric Current and Circuit
text:
Electric Current and Circuit

Key terms: electric current, electric charge, electric circuit

Electric current is the flow of electric charge, usually carried by electrons. It's expressed as the amount of charge flowing per unit time. An electric circuit is a continuous path for electric current.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electric Current and Circuit in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Electric Potential and Potential Difference
text:
Electric Potential and Potential Difference

Key terms: electric potential, potential difference, voltage, volts

Electric potential difference, or voltage, is the work done per unit charge to move an electric charge from one point to another. It's measured in volts (V).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Potential and Potential Difference in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Ohm's Law
text:
Ohm's Law

Key terms: Ohm's law, current, potential difference, resistance

Ohm's law states that the current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V) across it, provided its temperature remains constant. This relationship is expressed as V = IR, where R is the resistance of the conductor.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Ohm's Law in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Resistance of a Conductor
text:
Resistance of a Conductor

Key terms: resistance, length, area of cross-section, resistivity

The resistance of a conductor depends on its length (l), area of cross-section (A), and the nature of its material (ρ, resistivity). It's expressed as R = ρl/A.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Resistance of a Conductor in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Resistance and Current Dependence
text:
Resistance and Current Dependence

Key terms: resistance, current, potential difference

Resistance of a conductor depends on its length (R ∝ l) and cross-sectional area (R ∝ 1/A). Current depends on the resistance and potential difference (I = V/R).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Resistance and Current Dependence in Grade 10 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Science | Resistivity
text:
Resistivity

Key terms: resistivity, resistance

Resistivity (ρ) is a material property that determines its resistance. It is constant for a given material (R = ρl/A).

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Resistivity in Grade 10 Science.
